alerts.title: Geely BHE / i-HEV reaches 48.41% peak thermal efficiency
alerts.meta: GE HEV / PHEV engine Efficiency (#23, #25) · DieselNet, Apr 2026
alerts.body: Above the maximum of the adopted range. If confirmed on a homologated cycle, it favours HEV/PHEV and SPHEV over BEV on a cradle-to-grave basis.

alerts.title: Chery: 48% prototype (26:1, Miller cycle) and 44.5% in the production 1.5 TDGI
alerts.meta: GE HEV engine Efficiency (#23) and GE Compact (#18) · Auto Motor und Sport, Nov 2025
alerts.body: The production figure (44.5%) already exceeds the adopted maximum, suggesting the PET range for HEVs may be conservative.

alerts.title: Nissan e-POWER third generation: 1.5 turbo generator engine at ~42%
alerts.meta: Range Extender Combustion Engine Efficiency (#32) · InsideEVs Brasil
alerts.body: Within the range, above the most frequent value. Reinforces SPHEV/SHEV as a transition option.

alerts.title: Aramco Dedicated Hybrid Engine (DHE): 41% in a hybrid-dedicated engine
alerts.meta: Range Extender Combustion Engine Efficiency (#32) · Aramco Americas, 2026
alerts.body: Within the range. Relevant for emerging markets with biofuels — the Brazilian case.

alerts.title: CATL condensed-matter cell at 350 Wh/kg — a 125 kWh pack weighing ~625 kg (≈5.0 kg/kWh)
alerts.meta: Energy Battery Density reciprocal (#48) · Zecar, CATL Tech Day 2026
alerts.reported: ≈2.86 kg/kWh at cell level · ≈5.0 kg/kWh at pack level
alerts.body: The announced pack-level figure already approaches the adopted best case. It lowers BEV mass, pulling down both manufacturing and energy use — favours BEV.

alerts.title: Battery manufacturing: 50–100 kg CO2e/kWh typical, 10–25 with renewable electricity
alerts.meta: Energy Battery Carbon Intensity reciprocal (#62) · electrive, Aug 2025
alerts.body: The adopted minimum (44.1) sits far above what cells produced on a clean grid already achieve. Given the Brazilian low-carbon electricity mix, this is the parameter with the greatest potential to shift the result in favour of BEVs.

alerts.title: Stanford / Nature Energy: degradation up to 38% slower in real-world use; service life up to ~300,000 km
alerts.meta: Battery Lifespan (#55) and Usable Battery Capacity factor (#34) · Gadget Review (on the Stanford / Nature Energy study)
alerts.adopted: battery lifespan MF 200 · max 300 thousand km
alerts.body: Pushes battery lifespan towards the top of the range, diluting manufacturing emissions per km — favours BEV and PHEV.

alerts.title: Geotab (22,700 vehicles): average degradation of 2.3%/year, ~82% SoH after 8 years
alerts.meta: BEV lifetime-average Usable Battery Capacity factor (#34) · New Atlas / Geotab 2025
alerts.body: Suggests 0.75 is conservative for recent fleets. The i3ET has no explicit annual-degradation parameter — it is embedded in this factor.

notes: There is no explicit **annual capacity degradation (%/year)** parameter in the expert block. It is embedded in the lifetime-average usable capacity factor (#34 BEV, #35 PHEV). Tracking %/year directly would require creating the row.
There is no explicit **degradation after 200,000 km** parameter. The proxy is the combination of Vehicle Lifespan (#54), Battery Lifespan (#55) and factor #34.
Charging losses are split into **AC/slow (#36)** and **DC/fast (#37)**, weighted by the share of fast charging (#38) in the combined value (#39).

Reciprocal parameters (#48, #51, #53, #62, #65, #67) have min > max by construction — the minimum of the denominator becomes the maximum of the reciprocal. They are flagged as inverted ranges, not errors.
Parameters 106–113 appear under the LWP block but carry the group label "AUC" in the workbook — a labelling mismatch to be fixed at source.

history.text: Aug 3, 2026 — initial version. 120 parameters extracted from `LCA_LV_i3ET_20260724a.xlsx`. The alert baseline was built from the press review carried out for the paper (efficiencies of hybrid-dedicated engines and battery evolution). Recommendation column filled in: 14 parameters with a proposed adjustment or check, 106 recommended to keep.
